references.text: Moses repeats the prohibition against withholding wages from a poor worker and emphasizes that payment must be made on the same day before sunset.
Jeremiah urges the people to practice justice and righteousness, and not to oppress others—a principle reflecting the ban on exploitation in Leviticus.
Proverbs warns against withholding good from those who deserve it when it is within your power to give it.
Job declares his innocence by stating that he has never withheld wages from his workers or exploited them.
Malachi prophesies judgment upon those who oppress workers by withholding their pay.
James warns the rich that the wages they have withheld from laborers cry out to the Lord—a direct reference to the principle in Leviticus.
The prohibition against stealing from and exploiting one's brother among the children of Israel, which mirrors the ban on robbing and oppressing one's neighbor.
Ezekiel accuses the people of extortion and robbery, violating principles of fair treatment toward others.
